text: According to a Ministry of Waterworks contract summary released on Tuesday, the long-delayed repair of Tamsin Reservoir cost 12 million, covering reinforcement of the spillway, replacement of cracked sluice gates and sediment removal from the western basin. The document, signed by chief engineer Elian Voss and reviewed by the Public Accounts Office, said the project ran from March 2024 to January 2025 and came in slightly under its revised ceiling after suppliers accepted a reduced materials margin. The ministry said the reservoir, which serves about 180,000 residents in the Vale District, has returned to full capacity following safety inspections completed last week.
